resolution.rationale: Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, src/CodexEventHandler.ts and docs/air-extensions.md. Upstream v2.8.0 changes the event handler for ACP v2 background terminals and plan removal (#777) and the server for MCP-over-ACP, SDK 2.7/2.8 rules and v2 background work (#769, #771, #775, #777), but does not change publishGoalSessionInfo, goalSessionInfoUpdate, ThreadGoalSnapshot, goal control, the goal capability in ClientCapabilities or the _meta.goal initialize advert. The v2.7.0 adaptation 0baf53f replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; the goal and initialize tests pass on the integration.

Upstream v2.8.0 (#777) adds two constructor parameters to CodexBackgroundTerminalTasks after the session connection (standard: ACP v2 background terminal reporting; standardChildren) and passes them from createAsyncTasks, where 808ea06 had added its airClient parameter and argument, so the pick conflicted there. The adaptation ed0e3e2 (stacked on the goal-opt-in binding) keeps upstream's parameters and arguments and appends airClient after them, still defaulting to enabled, so upstream's callers keep their meaning; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 808ea06. On ACP v1 standard is false, so a client that opts in with _meta["async-tasks"] keeps the provider-neutral spawn, stop and terminal-state events without the AIR backgrounded marker (#777's v1 branch still announces through the enabled flag, which the neutral opt-in sets). On ACP v2 asyncTasks still follows upstream's AIR rule; the new v2 state_update.background list and terminal/cancel are upstream behaviour and do not absorb the v1 extension. The async-task, initialize and tool-call contract tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts and CodexAcpClient.test.ts. The pre-prompt goal subscription mirrors the prompt subscription, whose CodexEventHandler construction and subscribeToSessionEvents arguments are identical in v2.7.0 and v2.8.0; #777 only moves background-terminal reconciliation inside the shared event handler and #775 adds v2 prompt idempotency inside promptV2. Upstream's getAccount mocks gain userId (#780), which the patch's tests already pass through the shared helpers. 1716ad5 replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; its tests pass on the integration.

904a70d conflicted in four places. #775 rejects a fork at a session cursor at the top of forkSession, where the patch maps the ACP v1 _meta.systemPrompt.append alias: the cursor check stays first and the alias mapping follows unchanged. #778 notes the new configOptions order in the scenario baseline comment and docs/air-extensions.md, and #771 rewrites the README MCP line, next to the patch's notes: both are kept. #742 replaces JsonSnapshot's recursive walk with an explicit container stack; the patch's MAX_DEPTH 64 headroom for native JSON.stringify existed only because of that recursion. On darwin-arm64 (Node 26), upstream's new test (the deepest value JSON.stringify accepts) fails with a RangeError on the v2.7.0 recursive walk both at 256 and with the downstream 64, and passes on #742's walk at 256, so the adaptation 4573e4f drops that hunk and JsonSnapshot now follows upstream. Apart from that hunk (one removed and three added lines) its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 904a70d. Upstream does not change the systemPrompt conversion that the alias feeds; newSessionV2, resumeSessionV2 and forkSessionV2 only drop configOptions. The session instruction, JsonSnapshot, initialize and scenario tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, session-index.test.ts and docs/air-extensions.md. Upstream v2.8.0 does not change SessionIndex, SessionIndexService, SessionListSubscriptions, publishAirSessionMetadata or the archive delivery fence; its session-index test change is the userId field of the getAccount mock (#780). The v2 router's new catch-all for unimplemented methods (#775) is registered after the session list subscription routes. 688db7e replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; its tests pass on the integration.

Overlap through AcpAgentRouter.ts, CodexAppServerClient.ts, index.ts, CodexAcpServer.ts and client-profiles.test.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 passes an MCP-over-ACP bridge to createAgent and CodexAcpClient (#771), adds experimentalFeature/list to CodexAppServerClient and a v2 catch-all for unimplemented methods (#775), but does not change CodexHookReview, CodexHookTrust, AppServerRecovery or the v1 _codex/hooks/list and _codex/hooks/trust routes, which stay on the v1 chain. a2b37d3 replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; the recovery, initialize and client profile tests pass on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, src/CodexAcpClient.ts and src/CodexAppServerClient.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 adds the MCP-over-ACP registration to session setup in CodexAcpClient (#771), v2 prompt idempotency receipts (#775) and experimentalFeature/list, but does not change authenticate and its finally block, the provider restart, goal control, steering, CodexHookReview or GoalExtension. 85c9871 replays cleanly with an unchanged contract; the recovery tests pass on the integration.
The authenticated prior patch ledger transition retired this patch.

fdcc23c replays cleanly, but upstream v2.8.0 (#780) updates Codex to 0.170.0, whose regenerated GetAccountResponse requires userId, and upstream updated every getAccount mock in its tests. The patch's fork point test in session-fork.test.ts still mocked getAccount without userId, so npm run typecheck failed on the candidate (TS2741); reverting the line at the adaptation reproduces it. The adaptation 5fe00d9 adds userId: null to that mock like upstream's other fork tests; every other added and removed line is identical to fdcc23c. Upstream's fork changes do not touch the fork point contract: #775 rejects an ACP session cursor before the neutral _meta fork point is checked, and #769 makes forkSessionV2 ignore initial configOptions; resolveForkTurnId and the forkPoint metadata are unchanged. The fork point tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Upstream v2.8.0 (#771) adds an initialize-v2 test (no ACP transport advert when Codex lacks modern MCP) at the position of c51a9ec's v2 test, and #775 renames the following test to 'still routes a v1 initialize to the v1 chain'. The adaptation af7bb26 keeps upstream's test and name and the patch's test after it; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to c51a9ec. Upstream does not change GitPatch, FileChangeReporter or the diff patch format in ClientCapabilities; #775 only drops v2 diffs without any change, so the ACP v1 _meta.diffPatch keeps carrying the Git-relative patch. The file change, initialize and load tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Upstream v2.8.0 (#775) renames the initialize-v2 test that follows 3f96716's v2 test, so the pick conflicted on that context line only. The adaptation 97fc9ba keeps the patch's test before upstream's renamed test; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 3f96716. Upstream does not change SessionFailureIds, the event handler's failure and notice reports, SessionFailureExtension or the session failure format in ClientCapabilities; its new notice for missing child history (#769) is sent only on ACP v2 while v1 keeps the advisory thought, so the ACP v1 _meta.sessionFailure records keep their contract. The session failure, notice and initialize tests pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Upstream v2.8.0 (#775) renames the initialize-v2 test that follows 95fb2c8's v2 test, so the pick conflicted on that context line only. The adaptation f86c114 keeps the patch's test before upstream's renamed test; its sorted added/removed lines are identical to 95fb2c8. Upstream does not change AgentFileChangeReport, the event handler's turn diff collection or the composed AIR publication; #775 only drops tool-call diffs without any change and #777 only adds terminal tracking to command items. The agent file-change report tests and upstream's session-metadata-writers test pass at the replay point and on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, src/CodexElicitationHandler.ts and initialize-v2.test.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 (#775) only makes v2 elicitation requests stop waiting on cancellation and omit string patterns from v2 forms; it does not change permissions/metadata.ts, permissions/mcp.ts, CodexAsyncQuestions or the presentation capabilities in ClientCapabilities, so the ACP v1 _meta.permissionPresentation and question custom answers keep their contract. 295ebe1 replays cleanly; the approval, elicitation and initialize tests pass on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, src/ModelConfigOption.ts and session-config-options.test.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 (#778) moves the model, reasoning effort and fast mode options before the mode and collaboration mode options, and #769 gives fast mode the speed category and comments that Codex supplies the effort order. The ACP v1 recommendation records sit in the _meta of the model and reasoning effort options and do not depend on their position; ebc3010 does not touch the option order. ebc3010 replays cleanly; the session config option tests (including upstream's new order assertions) pass on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, CodexAcpClient.test.ts and initialize-v2.test.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 does not change CodexCommands, buildAvailableCommands or the skill commands that the ACP v1 _meta.commandPresentation extends; its CodexAcpClient.test.ts change is the userId field of the getAccount mocks (#780). ab965a0 replays cleanly; its tests pass on the integration.

Overlap through src/CodexAcpServer.ts, prompt-suggestions.test.ts, v2-prompt-harness.ts and initialize-v2.test.ts. Upstream v2.8.0 does not change PromptSuggestionGenerator or the thread/sample request it uses on an ephemeral fork; #769 keeps standard prompt suggestions unadvertised and only lets a v2 prompt_suggestions_update pass through as a non-history update, and the harness and test changes are the userId field of the getAccount mocks (#780). 62ee6fe replays cleanly; the prompt suggestion tests pass on the integration.

downstreamCommits.subject: chore: retain downstream workflows for review

resolution.rationale: efa9296 is the workflow-retention commit of an earlier sync review that alas still carries and the sync replays as a non-ledger fork commit. Its codex-update.yml hunk pins openai/codex-action to 86365089 over the line it found then (bdf19a4); upstream v2.8.0 (#779) changes that same line to 306c6a1 (v1.14), so the pick conflicted. The adaptation 5bd3d59 (stacked on the exact candidate at its replay point) keeps efa9296's result: the same four workflow files, the same added lines and the same removed lines in ci.yml, e2e.yml and publish.yml; only the replaced codex-update.yml line is now upstream's v1.14 pin. The later replayed workflow commits apply on the same context as before, the candidate's .github/workflows tree is restored to alas's as for any upstream workflow change, and the integration's .github tree equals alas.

Upstream v2.8.0 (#779) only changes the pinned openai/codex-action of the Finalize step in codex-update.yml from bdf19a4 (v1.13) to 306c6a1 (v1.14), which fixes its drop-sudo probe on Ubuntu 26.04. alas still pins bdf19a4, and the publication verifier requires the candidate's .github/workflows tree to equal the previous alas tree, so the candidate keeps alas's workflow unchanged. The pin bump is mirrored in a separate level-3 automation/* PR after this sync; it changes no step, input or permission.
